result:
I'd probably choose to shift how people process disagreement—to make it easier for people to genuinely understand views different from their own before dismissing them.

So much suffering seems to flow from talking past each other: polarization that prevents cooperation on shared problems, conflicts that escalate because each side feels unheard, resources wasted on fighting rather than solving.

I notice I'm drawn to this partly because it's a multiplier—if people actually understood each other better, they'd be better equipped to tackle climate change, inequality, health crises, all of it together rather than fractured.

Though I'm honestly uncertain whether this gets at root causes or just treats symptoms. Maybe the real issue is something else entirely—scarcity, how we're wired, institutional incentives. And genuine understanding doesn't always lead to agreement or cooperation either.

What would you choose? I'm curious whether you'd go for something concrete (poverty, disease) or something more structural like this.
